Figure 1:ReRound resolves ambiguous rounding with a learned diffusion prior.(a)The quantized floating-point weightw~=1.48\widetilde{w}=1.48is in the
midpoint ambiguity region (blue interval) in the
sense thatw~\widetilde{w}is sufficiently near the midpoint1.51.5.
As a result, there is low confidence on whetherw~\widetilde{w}should be
rounded down to the floor11or up to the ceiling22.
But, under RTN, becausew~\widetilde{w}is slightly closer to the floor11, in this case it will always be rounded to the floor.(b)For a given LLM, ReRound resolves midpoint ambiguity using a diffusion prior
(a U-Net) learned from64×6464{\times}64patches of all weight matrices in the
LLM.
Since this diffusion prior reflects the distribution of weights in the LLM,
ReRound uses it to guide the rounding.
In preparing for inference, the U-Net generates a collection of64×6464{\times}64patches aroundw~\widetilde{w}.
The generated patches will be designated as the reconstructedw~rec\widetilde{w}_{\mathrm{rec}}.
Sincew~rec\widetilde{w}_{\mathrm{rec}}reflects the distribution of weights of
the LLM, ReRound applies RTN tow~rec\widetilde{w}_{\mathrm{rec}}, rather thanw~\widetilde{w}, whenw~rec\widetilde{w}_{\mathrm{rec}}is not far fromw~\widetilde{w}.
Thus, in this example,w~=1.48\widetilde{w}=1.48under ReRound will be rounded to
the ceiling22rather than the floor11, as shown in (a).

The reconstructed weight in quantized space,w~rec\tilde{w}_{\mathrm{rec}}, proposes a change whenqrec=qaltq_{\mathrm{rec}}=q_{\mathrm{alt}}.
The proposal is accepted when its deviation fromw~\tilde{w}lies
within the position-dependent tolerance metricτpos​(r,τ)\tau_{\mathrm{pos}}(r;\tau); otherwise, RTN is retained.

Figure 7:Matrix-wise RTN revision rates for SmolLM2 1.7B.Each cell shows the percentage of RTN assignments revised by ReRound
for one weight matrix; lighter and darker colors indicate lower and
higher revision rates, respectively.
The revisions are distributed nonuniformly across network depth and
matrix type, and the W3 and W4 patterns differ despite reusing the same
reconstructed weights.
This shows that ReRound does not derive a fixed set of revisions from
the reconstruction alone.
Instead, each matrix is evaluated under its bit-specific quantization
grid and spectral preservation objective.
The same color scale is used in both panels.

Figure 8:Matrix-wise RTN revision rates for Llama 3.2 1B.Each cell shows the percentage of RTN assignments revised by ReRound
for one weight matrix; lighter and darker colors indicate lower and
higher revision rates, respectively.
Although W3 and W4 use the same reconstructed weights, they produce
different matrix-wise revision patterns.
ReRound evaluates the rounding candidates separately for each matrix
and bit width, and selects the candidate that best preserves the
leading singular values of the matrix.
The same color scale is used in both panels.
